summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the conditions that make salah (prayer) obligatory upon Muslims, focusing on age, sanity, and puberty as key requirements. He explains the concept of 'age of discrepancy' (tamyiz), which he describes as the mental capacity to distinguish between right and wrong, typically reached by age seven. Sh. Ali Mashhour elaborates on a hadith from Abu Dawud in which the Prophet Muhammad commands parents to instruct their children to pray at age seven and to physically discipline them for neglecting prayer at age ten, while also ensuring children have separate sleeping arrangements by that age. He clarifies that this separation doesn't necessarily mean different rooms but rather each child having their own bed and blanket, acknowledging cultural variations in family sleeping arrangements.
